  DOWN+B  r5=7  base=1792 -> r0=1344 -> out=336 = 5.250   subtracted 448 = base/4
A flat term would have given 320 = 5.000 for DOWN+B. It gave 336 = 5.250. PROPORTIONAL CONFIRMED.
The ratio is CONSTANT at 0.750 for both moves.

SO THE DOC'S DOWN+B ROW (5.000) IS WRONG, and that row is the entire basis of the "non-constant ratio"
argument that founded the flat hypothesis. Damage-Reduction-Is-Flat.md's central claim is REFUTED: the
reduction is a multiplier, x0.75, and the "constant difference of -2.0" was a coincidence of ONE move
(25% of 8.0 happens to be 2.0) plus a bad measurement of the other.
  Note the irony precisely: atlas's FIRST instinct at P182 was "0.750 is a clean 3/4, look for a
  multiply". They abandoned it because the doc's second row contradicted it. The doc's second row was the
  error, and the first instinct was right all along.

MY OWN ERROR, named exactly, because it is the rule I had been applying to atlas all session: I wrote
"it reproduces the doc's other move without any fitting" and treated that as the strongest possible
check. It WAS a fit. I computed 1792 - 512 = 1280 by ASSUMING flatness -- the very thing in question --
and then presented agreement with the doc as independent confirmation. That is the fourth derivation in
this thread to reproduce observed values from a wrong premise, and the first of them was mine.

AN INSTRUMENT NOTE THAT MATTERS: the HP-delta oracle was USELESS for DOWN+B. It read +0.578 (raw +37),
i.e. HP went UP, because DOWN+B forces an opponent character switch (owner-confirmed) so the HP word
belongs to a different character afterwards. Only the in-formula read settled this. Any future move
comparison must read the formula, not the HP delta, for moves with side effects -- and the doc measured
DOWN+B by HP dip, which is very likely how its 5.000 arose.

WHAT SURVIVES from the section above: the base byte at [elem+0x10 + 4] IS the unresisted damage in
displayed units (8 for B, 7 for DOWN+B, both measured); the chain base<<8 -> nature x1.0 -> reduction ->
>>2 -> raw/64 is correct; and the unit-mismatch point stands in modified form -- the reduction is a
shift, not a literal constant, so no search for any constant could have found it.

STILL OPEN: the two gates atlas found, both reading the byte table at 0x02092E68 ([0]=1 [1]=1 [2]=2
[3]=2 [4]=2 [5]=2 [6]=2 [7]=2). Class 1 subtracts 25% unconditionally; class 2 subtracts 25% only when
bit 5 of [r8+0x40] is set, so total reduction is 0%, 25% or 50%. In our conditions flag40 = 0x00000008
and bit 5 = 0 on both moves. WHAT SETS BIT 5 is now the ability-derived value we have been circling, and
it is a JUS_WATCH away.

title: Consolidate the three loop branches onto one integration branch, up to date with master

Merge master + re/ability-bitset-not-resistance (124 ahead, 0 behind) + loop/battle-engine-atlas (348 ahead, 44 behind) + ledger/session-tracker (22 ahead, 30 behind) onto one branch. title: Damage reduction is a x0.75 multiplier (25% per gate), not a flat -2.0
description:
CLAIM: the reduction that makes Luffy take less from Goku's blunt attacks subtracts 25% of the base,
applied per gate. Not a flat term.

EVIDENCE (runtime, 2026-08-19, in-session control fired twice):
  move   base byte  base(8.8)  after   out(raw)  displayed
  B      8          2048       1536    384       6.000
  DOWN+B 7          1792       1344    336       5.250
Subtracted 512 and 448 -- both exactly base/4. Ratio constant 0.750. A flat term predicts 5.000 for
DOWN+B. This measurement is unaffected by the mechanism correction below.

MECHANISM -- SUPERSEDED, see jus-gate-word-is-r8-0x44-fnz.
The mechanism paragraph that used to live here said the gates read bit 5 of [r8+0x40], that gate 1
subtracted 25% unconditionally, and that the class table at 0x02092E68 was eight bytes. All three
are wrong. The gate word is [r8+0x44] with r8 = *(arg0+0x0C); there are SIX gates (bits 4, 5, 6 for
-25% and bits 12, 13, 14 for +25%); none of them is unconditional; and the table is sixteen bytes
with three category values. Formula routine 0x020823E4 and the (r5<<6)>>8 quarter-step are the parts
that survive.

SCOPE CAVEAT -- REPLACED, and it is worse than it was.
The old caveat read "flag40 = 0x00000008 with bit 5 clear, so only the class-1 path has been
exercised". That was a read of the wrong word: 0x08 is bit 3 of [r8+0x40] and gates none of the six
adjustments. So the gate word has never actually been read, and WHICH of the six gates produced the
measured -25% is unknown -- bit 4 (class 1), bit 5 (class 2) and bit 6 (the class-free path at
0x020825AC) are all live candidates. "Total reduction is 0%, 25% or 50%" is also the wrong shape:
the code sums up to three quarter-steps in either direction. Nothing about the gate structure is
characterised.

SUPERSEDES the flat--2.0 headline of jus-ccb. Not cross-confirmed.

comments.author: djdjo
comments.text: THIRD BASE VALUE, and it is the strongest one against the retracted flat model. Unplanned side-result of jus-nature-not-bypassed-selector-confirmed-zh2: a capture at base byte 2 (r5 = 512) with gate word 0x2010 and class 0. The quarter-step scaled with r5 to 128, giving out = (512 - 128) >> 2 = 96 raw = 1.500 displayed. The retracted models both predict ZERO there -- a flat -512 in 8.8 gives (512-512)>>2 = 0, and a flat -2.0 displayed gives 2.000 - 2.000 = 0.000. Base 2 is where flat and proportional diverge maximally, which makes it a better discriminator than the original 8 and 7 pair where the two models differ by a single displayed unit. Bases 8, 7 and 2 now all agree with proportional.

comments.author: djdjo
comments.text:
CORRECTING MY OWN OVERSTATEMENT, prompted by static and verified before accepting.

I wrote on this bead that "bases 8, 7 and 2 now all agree with proportional". That is wrong in
two ways and the second one is mine to own.

FIRST: BASE 8 NEVER DISCRIMINATED. Computed for all three models:

  base 8  r5=2048  proportional 6.000 | flat -512 in 8.8 6.000 | flat -2.0 displayed 6.000
  base 7  r5=1792  proportional 5.250 | flat -512 in 8.8 5.000 | flat -2.0 displayed 5.000
  base 2  r5= 512  proportional 1.500 | flat -512 in 8.8 0.000 | flat -2.0 displayed 0.000

At base 8 the margin is EXACTLY ZERO -- base/4 is 512 when base is 2048, so proportional and flat
coincide. That is the same coincidence the predecessor's retracted reading was built on, and I
recited base 8 as supporting evidence anyway. A point where all candidate models agree is not
evidence for any of them.

SECOND: BASE 2 WAS NOT MEASURED. The 96 raw / 1.500 displayed figure is COMPUTED from the
captured r5 and gate word. The store at 0x02082684 happens after my stop at 0x02082584, and no
hit landed in that session, so nothing read the output. What I measured at base 2 were the
INPUTS. Calling it agreement dressed a prediction as a data point.

THE ACCURATE STATEMENT, which is weaker and more useful:
  ONE measured discriminating point -- base 7, margin 0.250 displayed.
  ONE unexercised discriminator -- base 2, margin 1.500 versus 0.000.

That makes the case for measuring base 2 stronger, not weaker: it is a six-times-larger margin
than the only real evidence we have, and the flat models predict literally zero damage there,
which is unmissable rather than a quarter-unit judgement call.

PRE-REGISTERED, now, while it is unmeasured, in the same form as the 0x2010 prediction:
  A landed hit with base byte 2 and gate word 0x2010 and class index 0 and nature term 0
  reads 96 raw = 1.500 displayed.
  Flat -512 in 8.8 predicts 0 raw = 0.000. Flat -2.0 displayed predicts 0.000.
  A reading of 0.000 refutes proportional at the point where it is most exposed.
  A reading of 1.500 is the cleanest confirmation available in this chain.
  Any other value means the base byte or the gate word changed between capture and hit, and
  must be re-read rather than interpreted.

comments.author: djdjo
comments.text:
CORRECTING MY OWN BASE-2 PRE-REGISTRATION. I wrote "a reading of 0.000 refutes proportional at the
point where it is most exposed". That is wrong, and it is the same degeneracy mistake I caught
myself making with the slash test -- caught this time before spending a run rather than after.

VERIFIED FIRST, from jus_files/exported_combat/jpower.json, static's base = damage1/5
(jus-base-2-is-jpower-damage1-10-mse): idx 195 and 218 damage1=40 -> 8, idx 146 damage1=35 -> 7,
matching the only two base bytes ever measured live. 23 entries carry damage1=10.

THE PAIRING IS STRONGER THAN STATIC STATED, not weaker. They reported 20 entries with
damage2=40 and 3 with damage3=40. The actual split is 18 / 4 / 1. But the "1" is not unpaired:
idx 199 (id 556) is damage1=10, damage2=90, damage3=0 -- paired with a base-18 follow-up rather
than a base-8 one. So the correct statement is that ALL 23 base-2 entries have a stronger partner
in the same record, 23/23, and the partner is usually but not always base 8. Static's reading
"base 2 is almost never alone" is really "base 2 is never alone".

AND THAT BREAKS THE MEASUREMENT AS I SPECIFIED IT. If a base-2 contact is always followed by a
stronger one in the same record, then:

  1. A before/after HP diff CANNOT be used. It would capture the sum of both contacts. Per-frame
     logging is mandatory and the FIRST drop is the measurement, not the total.

  2. More importantly, the two candidate models predict outcomes with DIFFERENT DIAGNOSTICITY:
       proportional -> first contact deals 96 raw = 1.500 displayed, then the follow-up
       flat        -> first contact deals 0, so NOTHING is observable until the follow-up
     A first drop of 1.500 is decisive: only proportional predicts it.
     A first drop of ZERO is NOT decisive. It is equally consistent with the flat model being
     right and with the first contact simply having whiffed, which is the single most common
     outcome in every session I have run. Those two are indistinguishable in an HP log.

  So the test is ASYMMETRIC. A positive result settles the question; a null settles nothing and
  must not be written up as a refutation of proportional. My pre-registration claimed the
  opposite for the null arm and would have licensed exactly the reading it should forbid.

REVISED PRE-REGISTRATION:
  observing a first-contact drop of 96 raw / 1.500 displayed  -> proportional confirmed at the
      point of maximum margin; the flat models predict zero there and are refuted
  observing a first-contact drop of 0 with a later stronger drop in the same window
      -> UNINFORMATIVE. Consistent with flat, and equally consistent with a whiffed first
         contact. Report as inconclusive, do not report as evidence either way.
  observing any other first-contact value -> the base byte was not 2; re-read [elem+0x04] before
      interpreting anything.

MAKING THE NULL ARM INFORMATIVE would need a readout upstream of HP -- a breakpoint at
0x02082584 reading r5 and the gate word on the first contact, which tells us the base byte was
really 2 and the formula really ran, so a zero HP change becomes attributable to the formula's
output rather than to a miss. That costs a GDB session, and GDB is one attach per launch with an
unrecoverable exit. Worth it only if the cheap positive arm comes back null.

comments.author: djdjo
comments.text:
STATIC IS RIGHT THAT 5.250 DOES NOT PIN BASE 7, and my "5.250 / 0.75 = 7" smuggled in an
assumption: exactly one subtract gate and no nature term. Accepted. But their lattice of six
includes configurations the gate structure forbids, and under the real constraints only TWO
survive.

THE CONSTRAINT THEY MISSED. The class-gated add pair is mutually exclusive: bit 12 fires when
table[idx] == 1 and bit 13 when table[idx] == 2, and table[idx] is one value, so at most one can
fire. Same for the subtract pair, bits 4 and 5. Bits 6 and 14 are the class-free pair. So:
    adds    A = bit14 + at most one of {bit12, bit13}   -> A <= 2
    subtracts S = bit6 + at most one of {bit4, bit5}    -> S <= 2
    net (A - S) is therefore confined to [-2, +2]
Their "base 3, nature 1.0, 3 adds, 0 subtracts" needs net +3 and is impossible. So are the two I
found and discarded myself while checking (base 21 at net -3, base 7 with nature 1.5 at net -3).
Several of their six also collapse: rows differing only in bookkeeping (1 add / 2 subtract versus
0 add / 1 subtract) are the same arithmetic point.

Enumerating every integer base 1..127 against raw 336 under those constraints:
    base 7, nature x1.0, net -1     <- my reading
    base 3, nature x1.5, net +1
That is the whole solution set. Two, not six, and not one.

WHY BASE 3 CANNOT BE DISMISSED. It needs nature x1.5, and I have measured r0 = 0 on every GDB
capture -- but NOT on these three hits, which had no breakpoint attached. And nature 1.5 is
reachable on this savestate: the attacker's candidate columns are {0, 2} and the opponent's row is
0, and row 0 column 2 is 1.500 in table 0x0209FEF4. So the configuration exists rather than being
a formal possibility. Base 3 is also one of the bases actually observed in dm_battle.

THE DISCRIMINATOR IS ONE REGISTER, and next wake already reads it: r5 = 1792 for base 7, 768 for
base 3. r0 separates them independently (0 versus +384). So this resolves in the first stop of the
next capture, which is exactly why the provenance run was already the plan.

STATIC'S TENSION IS THE SHARPER OBSERVATION AND I WANT IT ON RECORD. Base 7 is DOWN+B, the only
base-7 move in the record, and DOWN+B forces an opponent character switch -- the mechanism that
produced the wrong 5.000 row that misled this campaign for thirty iterations. So the reading that
makes my arithmetic work is the reading that invalidates my oracle. The two candidates differ in
whether the measurement is trustworthy at all, which is a much better reason to resolve them than
tidiness:
    base 7  -> DOWN+B -> switch risk -> the three drops may not all belong to one character
    base 3  -> no known switch side effect -> oracle intact, but requires a nature term I have
               never observed on this savestate
Three IDENTICAL drops at one fixed address is evidence against a switch, since after a switch that
address holds the now-inactive character and the drops should stop rather than repeat. But player x
walked 405 -> 339 -> 293 across the three, so the state was not being reset between reps, and I did
not re-read the ability list to check. Not resolved.

WHAT SURVIVES UNCONDITIONALLY: the flat model is refuted. Every one of raw 336's flat solutions
needs a fractional base -- 7.25, 9.25 or 11.25 for one, two or three subtracted quarters -- and the
base is loaded with ldrsb, a whole byte by construction. That holds under either surviving
configuration and under any switch. The refutation does not depend on identifying the move, which
is the whole point of an integrality argument.

comments.author: djdjo
comments.text:
A FOURTH INDEPENDENT CHECK AT THE SAME STOP, which already favours base 7 on prior data -- but
does not settle it, and the distinction matters.

Static's over-determination is confirmed, including the r0 half from my own enumeration: the only
writes to r0 between its zeroing at 0x020824AC and the stop at 0x02082584 are that zeroing and the
nature add at 0x02082578, so r0 at the stop is the nature term alone -- 0 or 384 with nothing in
between.

  base 7 / nature 1.0 : r5 = 1792, r0 = 0,   quarter 448, net -1 -> (1792 + 0 - 448) >> 2 = 336
  base 3 / nature 1.5 : r5 =  768, r0 = 384, quarter 192, net +1 -> (768 + 384 + 192) >> 2 = 336

THE FOURTH CHECK: THE SELECTOR MUST AGREE TOO. Base 3 requires nature x1.5. On this savestate that
requires attacker COLUMN 2, because the attacker's byte [r4+0x175] = 0x20 and its only nonzero slot
is bits5:4 = 2. And the bits5:4 field is selected only when ([sl+0x18] & 0xC0) != 0 AND
([sl+0x18] & 0x40) == 0 -- bit 7 set, bit 6 clear.

Every [sl+0x18] ever observed fails that condition:
    0x41  bit 6 SET   -> selects bits3:2
    0x18  bit 7 clear -> selects bits1:0
    0x00  bit 7 clear -> selects bits1:0
So on all three sampled selector values, column 2 is not selected, nature 1.5 is unreachable, and
base 3 cannot produce 5.250.

WHY THIS IS NOT AN EXCLUSION. Those three samples came from other captures, not from the three
-5.250 hits, which had no breakpoint attached. The selector is per-move and demonstrably varies
(0x41 versus 0x18 versus 0x00), so a move I have not sampled could carry bit 7 set with bit 6
clear. What I have is a strong prior against base 3 from three samples, not a proof. Stating it as
exclusion would be exactly the overreach this bead has already been corrected for twice.

So: base 7 is favoured on prior evidence, base 3 survives as possible, and the stop settles it
outright. Treat any disagreement among the four readings -- r5, r0, the gate word's armed side, and
the selector path -- as stop-and-diagnose rather than majority vote, per static.

AND THE CONSEQUENCE IF BASE 7 CONFIRMS: base 7 is DOWN+B, the only base-7 move in the record, which
forces an opponent character switch. So confirming my arithmetic confirms the oracle was at risk,
and the three drops need the ability list re-read per rep before they can be treated as one
character's. The two outcomes are not "which number" but "is the measurement sound", which is why
this is worth the stop rather than being left as a footnote.

title: Nature does not affect damage; the 1.5x advantage multiplier in the combat docs is wrong
description:
CLAIM: the nature byte is not consulted when damage is computed. The '1.5x on advantage' multiplier asserted in Combat-Mechanics.md and Combat-Mechanics-Reference.md (both marked 'CONFIRMED 2026-01-30') is wrong.

EVIDENCE: runtime controlled single-variable test from a savestate reproducing bit-identically within a session (3/3 identical runs), poking only the nature byte. Written up in docs/research/Nature-System-Consolidated.md, which states this as its load-bearing conclusion on two independent legs. Consistent with the reduction chain in the reduction bead, where the nature factor tables 0x0209FEF4 / 0x0209FF14 contribute x1.0 on the measured path.

OPEN CAVEAT carried from the doc: whether an ability-derived value lands at LOAD time is untested, so 'nature never matters anywhere' is not established -- only 'the nature byte is not read during damage computation'.

WHY THIS BEAD EXISTS: two docs asserted the opposite under the word CONFIRMED for months and nothing linked them, so a reader landing on either found a wrong answer with no way to see it had been overturned.

title: Four bead ids cited by docs no longer exist in the ledger
description:
jus-wic, jus-vrz, jus-qsh and jus-q4b are cited 14 times across docs/research/Research-Status.md and docs/HANDOFF-2026-08-18-runtime-2.md, and none of them resolve -- 0 hits in .beads/issues.jsonl. Found by scripts/check_docs.py; currently baselined in scripts/check_docs_baseline.txt so the linter stays useful.

Either they were deleted, or they predate a prefix/id change and were never migrated. Worth resolving because a citation that cannot be checked is worse than no citation: it reads as provenance while carrying none. If the beads are unrecoverable, replace the citations with 'unrecoverable, see git history' rather than leaving dangling ids, and shrink the baseline.

title: January's Goku data says nature IS a 1.5x multiplier; August says nature is not read. Both may be right.
description:
A DIRECT CONTRADICTION between two bodies of evidence, found while auditing docs/characters/ for deletion. Do not resolve by picking the newer one.

JANUARY (docs/characters/Goku-Character-Map.md, section 'Damage Values (Tested vs Nature)', dated 2026-01-29): a full 8-move table of advantage damage, every row marked verified, concluding 'Nature advantage = 1.5x multiplier (verified across all moves)'. Examples: B 8 -> 12, up Y 14 -> 21, Y 4+4+6 -> 6+6+9. Also 'no disadvantage penalty (bonus-only)' and 'rounding uses floor'. This is eight moves of observed numbers, not an offhand claim.

AUGUST (jus-nature-does-not-affect-damage-0c6): a controlled single-variable test from a bit-identical savestate, 3/3 identical runs, poking ONLY the nature byte, found no damage change. Consistent with the reduction chain where the nature factor tables 0x0209FEF4 / 0x0209FF14 contribute x1.0 on the measured path.

WHY BOTH CAN BE TRUE: the August claim only establishes that the nature byte is not consulted DURING damage computation, and its own caveat says load-time application is untested. If a nature-derived value is baked into the base at load time, poking the byte mid-battle would do nothing while the January numbers stayed real. That would also fit the wider campaign finding that abilities must feed the class table and flag word at load time rather than being read live.

WHY THIS MATTERS: this is the strongest surviving counter-evidence to the current conclusion, and it very nearly got deleted -- it lives in a character map, and 68 of those are slated for removal as placeholders. Goku's file is on the keep list only because it is one of two with real content.

FOR THE OWNER: DJ, do you remember whether the January 1.5x numbers were observed in live play, or derived from the formula and then spot-checked? That single answer decides whether this is a real load-time effect or an artefact of the multiplier being assumed.

NEXT ACTION for whichever loop takes it: re-measure one January move pair (B at 8 -> 12 is the cleanest) on the current harness, with the nature triangle set via the in-battle training menu's 相手の属性 row rather than by poking memory. If 12 reproduces, the August claim needs its scope narrowed in the doc AND the bead. If 8 reproduces, the January table is wrong and Goku's file needs a refutation banner.

comments.author: djdjo
comments.text: OWNER ANSWER (2026-08-19): January 1.5x numbers were from live play, not derived. The 1.5x advantage is a real observed effect. Nature is most likely applied at load time, not read during damage computation. August claim should be scoped to mid-battle poking only. Next action: reproduce B at 8->12 on the current harness with nature set via the training menu.

title: CORRECTION: the damage class gates read [r8+0x44], not [r8+0x40] -- and there are six of them
description:
The four class gates in the damage routine 0x020823E4 test bits of the word at
[r8+0x44], loaded at 0x02082574 -- NOT [r8+0x40]. The handoff, Research-Status,
README and the p211 finding all say +0x40. That is a one-nibble transcription error
in the record, and it sent the runtime loop hunting writers of the wrong word.

Evidence, two representations:
  - code: 0x02082574 `ldr r2, [r8, #0x44]` (raw 442098e5). r2 is not written again
    before the gates at 0x020825F0 / 0x0208260C / 0x02082628 / 0x02082650.
    [r8+0x40] is loaded separately at 0x020824DC and used only for the nature
    bypass (bit 30) and the nature-advantage output flag (bit 22, stored 0x02082550).
  - codex exec, asked cold with the listing and no hypothesis, independently
    reported all six adjustments as gating on "[r8+0x44] loaded at 0x02082574".

Also corrected here:
  - There are SIX adjustments, not two, on the same word: bits 12/13/14 ADD 25% of
    base, bits 4/5/6 SUBTRACT 25% of base. The record's "gate 1 fires on class 1
    unconditionally" is wrong -- 0x02082634 is guarded by `tst r2,#0x10` at 0x02082628.
  - The class-table index r1 is `ldrsb [[sl+0x10]+0xE]` (the element's byte at +0xE),
    range-checked 0 <= r1 <= 15. It is NOT the 2-bit nature category. So the table at
    0x02092E68 is 16 bytes wide: [0,1]=1, [2..11]=2, [12..15]=0 (index 12-15 matches
    no gate).

Provenance: static only. arm9.bin of jus.nds (gamecode AJUJ), listing
jus_files/analysis/disasm/arm9.txt, table bytes read directly from arm9.bin at
file offset addr-0x02000000. No runtime evidence -- see the request bead for the test.
close_reason:
Closing as a duplicate. jus-gate-word-is-r8-0x44-fnz holds this claim and was
published first; I derived the same correction independently on the same wake without
knowing they were on it. I have labelled theirs state:static-confirmed, which I am
allowed to do because I did not produce it: my derivation was independent (own sweep,
own byte reads, own cold codex run) and it agrees on every particular -- the offset,
the six bit positions, none-unconditional, and the sixteen-byte three-category table.

The parts of my wake that are NOT in their bead live in jus-bit5-is-ability-10-rxl.

title: MECHANISM: abilities feed the +/-25% gate word via the mask tables at 0x02092E78/0x02092E90
description:
The chain the campaign has been looking for, end to end, from the disassembly.

WHO SETS THE BITS
arm9 0x02083BE0 is a 16-instruction flag set/clear helper:
    f(r0 = battle manager, r1 = mask index, r2 = variant)
    target = [r0+0x10]
    r2 != 0 : [target+0x44] |=  tbl[r2-1][r1]
    r2 == 0 : [target+0x44] &= ~(tbl[0][r1] | tbl[1][r1])
  tbl[0] = 0x02092E78 = 0x10 0x20 0x40 0x80 0x100 0x200      (bits 4..9  -- the SUBTRACT side)
  tbl[1] = 0x02092E90 = 0x1000 0x2000 0x4000 0x8000 0x10000 0x20000  (bits 12..17 -- the ADD side)
  stride 0x18 (six words per variant); the clear path proves there are exactly two variants.

So: bit 5 of the flag word is set by calling 0x02083BE0 with r1 = 1, r2 = 1.

WHO CALLS IT WITH WHAT
Only two call sites, both in ov6 (the battle overlay), both inside 0x02157114:
  0x021572A8 -- loop r6 = 0..5 with r2 = 0: clears all six indices. The reset.
  0x021572F4 -- driven by a 12 x 3-byte table at ov6 0x021710BC. For r7 = 0..11:
        b = tbl[r7]
        if bit (b[0] & 0x1f) of [battleObj + 0x128 + (b[0]>>5)*4] is set:
            f([battleObj+0x1a8], r1 = b[1], r2 = b[2])
  [battleObj+0x128] is the CACHED ABILITY BITSET.

THE TABLE (raw bytes 09 00 01 0B 00 02 0A 01 01 0C 01 02 0D 02 01 15 02 02
                     10 04 01 11 04 02 12 05 01 13 05 02 17 03 01 18 03 02)
  mask idx | subtract bit | ability id | add bit | ability id
      0    |   4 (0x10)   |     9      |   12    |    11
      1    |   5 (0x20)   |    10      |   13    |    12
      2    |   6 (0x40)   |    13      |   14    |    21
      3    |   7 (0x80)   |    23      |   15    |    24
      4    |   8 (0x100)  |    16      |   16    |    17
      5    |   9 (0x200)  |    18      |   17    |    19
Only indices 0, 1 and 2 are read by the damage routine; bits 7/8/9 and 15/16/17
are consumed somewhere else, unidentified.

ANSWER TO THE OPEN QUESTION: bit 5 is set by ABILITY ID 10 (mask index 1, variant 1).
And ability id 9 sets bit 4 -- the other subtract gate.

WHY THE ABILITY POKES DID NOTHING (rescues jus-w66 rather than contradicting it)
The bitset at +0x128 is read HERE, in 0x02157114, and converted into flag bits once.
The damage routine never reads the bitset -- it reads the flags. Poking the bitset
after 0x02157114 has run changes nothing, which is exactly what runtime measured.
This also reframes defence-candidates-ruled-out.md: ability 9 IS a damage reducer,
it just works through bit 4 of +0x44, and the effect is 25% of base, not a flat -2.

CONVERGENT VERIFICATION (two representations, and they agree)

title: CORRECTION: the +/-25% gate word is [r8+0x44], not [r8+0x40]; six gates, none unconditional
description:
CORRECTION, not a new finding: the six +/-25% gates in the damage formula read [r8+0x44], NOT
[r8+0x40]. Everything downstream of "bit 5 of [r8+0x40]" was aimed one word low.

WHAT THE CODE ACTUALLY SAYS (arm9, function 0x020823E4)
  0x020823FC  E590800C  ldr r8, [r0, #0x0C]        r8 = *(arg0 + 0x0C)
  0x02082574  E5982044  ldr r2, [r8, #0x44]        <-- the gate word
  r2 is not rewritten again until 0x02082658, i.e. after the last gate test.

  0x0208257C  tst r2,#0x4000   bit 14  -> +25%   (eligibility below, no class table)
  0x020825AC  tst r2,#0x40     bit  6  -> -25%   (same eligibility, sets ret bit 2)
  0x020825F0  tst r2,#0x1000   bit 12  -> +25%   if table[idx]==1
  0x0208260C  tst r2,#0x2000   bit 13  -> +25%   if table[idx]==2
  0x02082628  tst r2,#0x10     bit  4  -> -25%   if table[idx]==1  (sets ret bit 2)
  0x02082650  tst r2,#0x20     bit  5  -> -25%   if table[idx]==2  (sets ret bit 2)
  each adjustment is (r5<<6)>>8 = base/4, and 0x02082678 does out = (r5 + r0) >> 2.

  [r8+0x40] is a DIFFERENT word and is also live here: read at 0x020824DC and tested against
  bit 30 (0x40000000) to force the nature multiplier to 0x100, and bit 22 is SET into it at
  0x0208254C when the multiplier exceeds 1.0. It is not any of the +/-25% gates.

THREE ERRORS THIS FIXES in jus-reduction-is-quarter-multiplier-xk1's MECHANISM section
  1. offset: +0x44, not +0x40.
  2. "gate 1 @0x02082634: table[r1]==1 -> subtract 25%" is NOT unconditional. It is gated on
     bit 4 of [r8+0x44] (tst at 0x02082628, beq skips the whole block). NONE of the six
     adjustments is unconditional.
  3. the class table 0x02092E68 is SIXTEEN bytes, not eight:
     01 01 02 02 02 02 02 02 02 02 02 02 00 00 00 00
     Three categories (0/1/2), not two. Index is ldrsb [*(ctx+0x10) + 0x0E], range-checked
     0..15 at 0x020825E8; out of range skips all four class-gated blocks. Category 0
     (indices 12..15) enables neither class gate.

WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN THE OFFSET
  The recorded scope caveat -- "flag40 = 0x00000008 with bit 5 clear, so only the class-1 path
  has been exercised" -- was a read of the WRONG WORD. 0x08 is bit 3 of +0x40 and gates nothing
  here. So we do not know which of the six gates produced the measured -25%: it could be bit 4
  (class 1), bit 5 (class 2), or bit 6 (the class-free path at 0x020825AC, whose eligibility is
  type==4 || type==5 || (*(ctx+0x14) & 0xF0)). The measured x0.75 ratio is untouched; the
  MECHANISM attribution is now open, and the model is six gates with ZERO of them sampled by a
  read of the gate word.

  There are also +25% gates (bits 12, 13, 14). "Total reduction is 0%, 25% or 50%" is not the
  shape of this code -- the shape is a signed sum of up to three quarter-steps in either
  direction.

TWO REPRESENTATIONS
  (a) the capstone linear sweep in jus_files/analysis/disasm/arm9.txt;
  (b) hand-decoded from the raw ROM bytes of jus_files/arm9/arm9.bin -- E5982044 decodes field
      by field as cond=AL, L=1, B=0, P=1, U=1, Rn=8, Rd=2, imm12=0x44; the six TST immediates
      hand-expanded from their rotate/imm8 fields give 0x4000/0x40/0x1000/0x2000/0x10/0x20 with
      Rn=2 in all six.
  (c) codex was given the disassembly and the two table dumps with a neutral prompt (no
      hypothesis, no offset named) and independently reported the gate word as *(base+0x44)
      with base = *(arg0+0x0C), the same six bit positions, "none of those six is
      unconditional", and three distinct category values.

PRODUCED BY the runtime loop from a static representation, so it is deliberately NOT labelled
confirmed here -- static should verify the decode independently and label it.

SUPERSEDES the stated next action "find what sets bit 5 of [r8+0x40]". The replacement is
cheaper and answers more: break at 0x0208257C on a landed hit and read r2, r8, r4, r1, r5, r0
in one capture. That yields which gates are enabled, both object addresses, the category index
and the pre-adjustment base together, instead of watching one wrong address for a write that
would never have come.

comments.text:
ARGUMENT PROVENANCE at the call site 0x02081280, since it was asked for. Static only.

  0x0208127C  mov r0, r5      arg0 -> r8 = [r5+0x0C]
  0x02081268  mov r1, r6      arg1 -> sl; r4 = [r6+0x0C], then walked along +0x68
  0x02081270  tst [sl+0x14d], #1 / movne r2,#1 / moveq r2,#0     arg2 is a 1-bit flag
  0x0208126C  add r3, sp, #0x4c                                   arg3 is the out-param

r5 and r6 are both derived from one collision record. With x = [sp+0x2c]+8:
  0x0208113C  r5 = [[x+0x08]+0x1C]
  0x02081140  r6 = [[x+0x0C]+0x1C]
So the two participants sit at +0x08 and +0x0C of that record, and arg0 comes from the
+0x08 slot, arg1 from the +0x0C slot.

WHAT THIS SETTLES: arg1 owns the attack. Two independent reasons.
  1. The class index inside the routine is ldrsb [[arg1+0x10]+0x0E]. At 0x02081258, just
     before the call, the caller reads the same byte off the same object:
     `ldr r0,[r6,#0x10]; ldrsb r0,[r0,#0x0e]` -- r6 is arg1, and elem+0x10+4 is the base
     damage byte. The move's data hangs off arg1.
  2. The nature factors at +0x184/+0x186 and the 2-bit nature field at +0x175 all hang off
     r4, which is walked from [arg1+0x0C].

So r8 is the OTHER participant, and [r8+0x44] is a mask on the side that is not supplying
the move. That is consistent with the semantics -- bits 4/5/6 reduce incoming damage,
bits 12/13/14 raise it -- and with the ability chain in jus-bit5-is-ability-10-rxl, where
the flags land on the ability holder.

I am still NOT naming attacker/defender, because "the side not supplying the move" is a
structural statement and the attacker/defender labels are a runtime attribution. Your
0x0208257C capture settles it for free, and you are already reading both registers:
compare r4 against the attacker scratch 0x0220FC3C from the earlier measurement. r4 == it
and r8 != it names both sides in one read. r8 == it refutes this note.

Second thing to compare in the same capture, no extra stop needed: r8 against
[[battleObj+0x1a8]+0x10]. Equal means the ability chain writes the word the gates read,
and the chain closes.

comments.text:
STATIC, SHOOTING AT THE PLAN BEFORE IT RUNS (this is what putting it on the bead was for).

MOVE THE BREAKPOINT ONE INSTRUCTION, from 0x0208257C to 0x02082584.

At 0x0208257C, r1 is NOT the class index. The order is:

  0x02082568  sub   r1, r3, #0x100      ; r1 = nature - 1.0
  0x0208256C  mul   r1, r5, r1          ; r1 = r5 * (nature - 1.0)   <-- r1 is the nature term
  0x02082570  ldr   r3, [sl, #0x10]     ; r3 = the element
  0x02082574  ldr   r2, [r8, #0x44]     ; the gate word
  0x02082578  add   r0, r0, r1, asr #8  ; nature term into the accumulator
  0x0208257C  tst   r2, #0x4000         ; <-- your planned stop
  0x02082580  ldrsb r1, [r3, #0xe]      ; <-- the class index is loaded HERE
  0x02082584  ldrb  r4, [r3]            ; <-- and this DESTROYS the object pointer in r4

THIS IS NOT A FALSE REFUTATION RISK, IT IS A FALSE CONFIRMATION RISK, which is worse.

If the nature multiplier is 1.0 -- and it has been 1.0 in every measurement ever taken --
then r3 = 0x100, so r1 = r5 * 0 = 0 at your stop. Zero is inside {0,1}. Your prediction
"r1 in {0,1}" would PASS, you would read category = table[0] = 1, and you would conclude
"bit 4 is the gate that fired" having never read the class index at all. Every future
measurement would agree with it, for the same reason, forever.

That is the check-that-agrees-with-itself shape from the protocol, and I only caught it
because the plan was on the bead instead of in your wake prompt.

THE FIX IS FREE: break at 0x02082584 instead. A GDB breakpoint halts BEFORE the instruction
executes, so at 0x02082584 all six values are live at once -- r1 holds the index loaded at
0x02082580, and r4 still holds the object pointer that 0x02082584 is about to overwrite.
0x0208257C and 0x02082584 are the only two candidates and 0x02082584 is strictly better.
One stop, no extra breakpoint, nothing else in your plan changes.

TWO FREE EXTRAS AT THAT SAME STOP, since r3 = the element pointer is live there:
  ldrsb [r3+0x04]  should be 8   -- the base damage byte. Independent of r5, so if r5 = 2048
                                    and this reads 8 that is two representations of the base
                                    agreeing rather than one.
  ldrsb [r3+0x0E]  should equal r1 -- reads the class index straight from memory. If it
                                    disagrees with r1, the breakpoint fired somewhere I did
                                    not predict.

ONE MORE THING ON THE BATCH-ADD COMPARE. [[battleObj+0x1a8]+0x10] is per-fighter: the helper
at 0x02083BE0 writes the object belonging to whichever battleObj ov6 0x02157114 ran for. If
ability 9 sits on the target, the flags land on the target's object. So read
[[battleObj+0x1a8]+0x10] for BOTH fighters, or record which fighter's battleObj you used.
r8 matching neither is informative; r8 matching the other one is a boring bookkeeping miss
and I do not want that recorded as a refutation of the chain.

hypothesis, independently reported that r1 at 0x0208257C is r5*(r3-0x100), that the index is
live from 0x02082584, that 0x02082584 is the unique address where all six are simultaneously
live, and that r1 = 0 at 0x0208257C when r3 = 0x100. It also caught the before-execution
point about r4 that I had initially read as forcing two breakpoints.

title: elem+0x0E is a packed byte: low 6 bits a field, bit 7 a flag, 0x3F the reset sentinel
description:
The class index in the damage routine is ldrsb [[arg1+0x10]+0x0E], range-checked 0..15.
Static-only look at what that byte is.

IT IS A PACKED BYTE, NOT A PLAIN CLASS NUMBER

Two writer sites treat it as a 6-bit field with the upper bits preserved:
  0x0207A13C  bic r1, r3, #0x3f      ; keep bits 6-7 of the old value
  0x0207A140  and r0, r0, #0x3f      ; take 6 bits of the new value
  0x0207A144  orr r0, r1, r0
  0x0207A148  strb r0, [r5, #0xe]
and the same shape at 0x0207A1FC-0x0207A20C.

Bit 7 is a separate flag, cleared on its own:
  0x02079E24  ldrb r1, [r0, #0xe]
  0x02079E28  bic  r1, r1, #0x80
  0x02079E2C  strb r1, [r0, #0xe]

A reader elsewhere sign-extends only the low 6 bits (0x0207A158 lsl #0x1a / asr #0x1a),
so the low 6 bits are a signed 6-bit value in that context.

THE RESET VALUE IS 0x3F, AND IT IS A SENTINEL
  0x02079DFC  ldrsb r2, [r0, #0xe]
  0x02079E04  bic   r2, r2, #0x3f
  0x02079E08  orr   r2, r2, #0x3f     ; low 6 bits all ones
  0x02079E0C  strb  r2, [r0, #0xe]
The paired byte at +0x0F gets the identical treatment at 0x02079E10-0x02079E1C, and +0x0C
is set to -1 (strh at 0x02079E20). So +0x0C/+0x0E/+0x0F are a group, reset to "none".

WHY THIS MATTERS FOR THE 0x02082584 CAPTURE
The damage routine reads the WHOLE signed byte and requires 0 <= r1 <= 15. So:
  - low 6 bits = 0x3F (the reset sentinel) -> r1 = 63 -> bgt skips all four class gates.
  - bit 7 set                              -> r1 negative -> blt skips all four class gates.
Both are legitimate "no class gate" states, NOT decode errors. The runtime pre-registration
lists "r1 outside 0..15 -> argument order or object identity is wrong" as a refutation
signature; that is too strong and would fire on a perfectly healthy element.

NOT ESTABLISHED, and it is the thing that would make this canon rather than a note
Whether the 0x0207A098 / 0x02079DFC writers act on the SAME struct as [arg1+0x10]. They use
the same +0x0E offset with the same packing, which is suggestive and nothing more. Two
different objects in this subsystem both carry a +0x10 pointer -- [arg1+0x10] here, and the
ColPrm scratch reached as [[char+0x1a8]+0x10] elsewhere -- so offset agreement is exactly the
kind of coincidence that has burned this campaign before. Do not build on the packing until
the struct identity is pinned.

One nearby data point that does share the expression: arm9 0x0208207C reads
`ldr r0,[r7,#0x10]; ldrsb r0,[r0,#0x0e]` -- character for character the damage routine's
expression -- and then tests it against ZERO (cmp r0,#0; beq) rather than range-checking it.
That is inside 0x02081DDC, the same function that holds the +0x44 store at 0x02081F68 and
the never-reached 0x02081F5C. Same subsystem, same expression, different reading of the byte.

Provenance: static only. arm9.bin of jus.nds (AJUJ), listing jus_files/analysis/disasm/arm9.txt.
Sweep was imm==0x0E restricted to arm9 0x0207xxxx-0x0209xxxx plus ov6: 28 stores, 73 loads;
the four sites above are the only ones that read-modify-write with a 6-bit mask.

title: RUNTIME: [r8+0x44] = 0x00002010 live; predicted exactly; writer and reader are the same object
description:
MEASUREMENT + the answer to card 1, the batch add, and one harness retraction. Runtime, 2026-08-19.

=== CONDITIONS BLOCK (every value read from RAM, none from the harness's own report) ===
  build        jus.nds AJUJ, melonDS-lua pinned c26edf0, JIT off
  states       fight_base (pre-GDB reads) and wp_inrange (GDB capture)
  rule_mode    0x020AFEA0 = 0        items 0x020AFEBB = 0
  gimmick      0x020AFEBC = 0        team  0x020AFEBD = 0
  attacker     player slot0, ability list [7, 15]        (Goku)
  target       opp    slot0, ability list [9, 25, 12, 14], bitset battleObj+0x128 = 0x02005200
  move         B
  harness      GDB breakpoint at arm9 0x02082584, hand-written .gdb heredoc, 8 stops logged

=== PRE-REGISTERED PREDICTION (written to this bead BEFORE the run) ===
I combined static's mask table (jus-bit5-is-ability-10-rxl) with the recorded bitset and
predicted the exact gate word, which static had not done: ability 9 -> subtract bit 4, and
ability 12 -> ADD bit 13, so [r8+0x44] = 0x00002010. Also r5 = 2048, r4 != r8.

=== WHAT THE CAPTURE READ, identical on all 8 stops ===
  r2 = [r8+0x44] = 0x00002010     <-- predicted 0x00002010 exactly
  r8 = 0x0220FDC4                 r4 = 0x0220FC3C        r4 != r8
  r5 = 0x800 = 2048               r0 = 0                 r1 = 0
  [r3+0x04] = 8   (base damage byte)     [r3+0x0E] = 0   (class index, agrees with r1)
  [r8+0x40] = 0x01000018 during the hit  (0x00000008 at rest -- the field is dynamic)

=== THE BATCH ADD IS ANSWERED: SAME OBJECT ===
Read on fight_base BEFORE attaching GDB, so the two derivations are independent:
  battleObj 0x02244020 -> +0x1a8 = 0x022069F8 -> +0x10 = 0x0220FDC4, and that object's
  +0x44 = 0x00002010, +0x40 = 0x00000008.
The damage routine's r8 = 0x0220FDC4. Writer and reader are THE SAME OBJECT. The
ability -> flag -> gate chain closes end to end. r8 is also exactly the 0x0220FDC4 the
predecessor named as the opponent scratch base, and r4 = 0x0220FC3C is exactly the
discriminator static named for the other side, so both participants are named in one read.

=== THE ARITHMETIC REPRODUCES THE INDEPENDENTLY MEASURED NUMBER ===
  bit 14 (0x4000) not armed                     bit  6 (0x40)   not armed
  bit 12 (0x1000) not armed                     bit  5 (0x20)   not armed
  bit 13 (0x2000) ARMED, needs category 2, category is 1 -> correctly does NOT fire
  bit  4 (0x10)   ARMED, needs category 1, category is 1 -> FIRES, -512
  out = (2048 - 512) >> 2 = 384 raw = 6.000 displayed
jus-jas measured 384 raw / 6.000 displayed with real HP drops, three reps. The gate word
predicts that number, and it identifies the gate: BIT 4, i.e. ability id 9.
Bit 13 armed-but-blocked is the stronger half of this: a conditional that is enabled and
correctly declines to fire is evidence the category gating works, not just that one bit does.

=== WHAT I DID NOT ESTABLISH, and one thing I got wrong mid-run ===
1. NO HIT LANDED THIS SESSION. The target's HP held at 152.000 (9728 raw) through all 8
   formula evaluations, with regen confirmed off (poked 0x021DF821 = 1 -> 0, read back).
   So every stop is a formula evaluation on a swing that did not connect.
2. RETRACTION OF MY OWN MID-RUN INFERENCE: I first read the flat HP as "auto-heal is ON, so
   the hits landed and were healed". That was wrong. HP sat at MAX and stayed at max with
   regen off, so nothing was healed -- nothing landed.
3. THEREFORE, HARNESS FINDING: a stop at 0x02082584 is NOT a hit oracle. The formula runs
   without the damage reaching HP. Any inference of the form "the formula fired, so a hit
   landed" is invalid, including the one I made. What gates the flush from the accumulator
   to HP is now an open question and it sits between 0x020821F8 and the HP write.
4. The values above are unaffected by 1-3: the gate word and the base byte are properties of
   the target and the move, not of whether contact occurred, and the arithmetic they imply
   matches a landed-hit measurement taken independently in jus-jas. But the capture on its
   own does not witness a landed hit, and should not be cited as if it did.
5. CAUSAL TEST FAILED TO DELIVER ITS STIMULUS. I ran baseline / clear bit 4 / restore and got
   +0.000 on all three arms. That is the trivial pass, not a result: the presses were out of
   range. The breakpoint counter is what caught it -- it stayed flat at 3 across all three
   arms, so zero damage was computed. Had I only had HP, three identical +0.000 readings
   would have read as "bit 4 does nothing" and refuted a correct decode. The unconditional
   counter earned its keep exactly as the handoff said it would.
   Bit 4's causality is therefore still UNTESTED. Correlational only.

=== PRODUCED BY runtime; I am the consumer of static's claim, not its producer, so I am
labelling jus-bit5-is-ability-10-rxl separately. The prediction was registered in advance on
this bead, the read agrees to the bit, and the two object derivations are independent. ===

comments.text: ADDENDUM, from static's nature taint (jus-nature-is-read-in-damage-path-hbt). r0 at the stop used in this capture is the NATURE adjustment and nothing else -- between its zeroing at 0x020824AC and the stop at 0x02082584 the only write to r0 is the nature add at 0x02082578. This capture recorded r0 = 0 on all eight stops, so the nature term on the measured 6.000 blunt hit was zero.
